answer: A device proves it shares a lived-in room by recording the indoor carbon dioxide curve: people exhale, so CO2 climbs through the evening and falls when windows open, a small sensor logging every breath of the household. A Sybil farm cannot fake this, because the curve must match the room's real occupancy rhythm, and a karst cave, a dune cabin and a hall floored in onyx each ventilate differently. No script can predict that shape without actually being there.
